nodes.title: Amazon S3: Key Ideas
nodes.content: S3 is AWS's object store — flat namespace of buckets containing objects, accessed via HTTP. It backs almost every AWS architecture: data lakes, static sites, backups, lambda triggers, CloudFront origins. The exam tests storage classes, encryption, access control, and event notifications.

flashcards.front: S3 storage classes — pick one for backups, one for hot data, one for archive.
flashcards.back: Hot: S3 Standard (high cost, instant access). Backups / infrequent: S3 Standard-IA (cheaper storage, retrieval fee). Archive: Glacier Deep Archive (cheapest storage, retrieval in hours). Lifecycle policies move objects between classes automatically based on age.

flashcards.front: S3 bucket policy vs IAM policy vs ACL — which to use?
flashcards.back: IAM policy: 'this user/role can read bucket X'. Bucket policy: 'these principals can access this bucket' — required for cross-account and public access. ACL (legacy): per-object permissions, mostly avoided today. Use bucket policies for most cross-account, IAM for in-account.

flashcards.front: How do you make an S3 website (static-site hosting)?
flashcards.back: Enable static-website hosting on the bucket, upload index.html, set a bucket policy allowing public-read on objects, point a CloudFront distribution at it for HTTPS + edge caching. Don't expose the bucket directly — CloudFront with an OAC (Origin Access Control) is the canonical pattern.

flashcards.front: What's the difference between server-side and client-side encryption?
flashcards.back: SSE: data encrypted by S3 after upload. Variants: SSE-S3 (AWS-managed key, easiest), SSE-KMS (your KMS key, audit trail), SSE-C (you supply the key on each request). Client-side: you encrypt before upload — S3 only sees ciphertext. Pick SSE-KMS for compliance, SSE-S3 for default-on.

pairs.stem: A global software vendor needs to publish product documentation, images, and downloadable PDFs for a product launch microsite. The 3 GB file set is updated roughly once per month and must load quickly for visitors across North America, Europe, and Asia-Pacific. The team has no dedicated server administrators and must minimize both cost and ongoing operational effort. Which architecture meets these requirements?
pairs.option: Host the assets in S3 and distribute them through a CloudFront distribution with edge caching

pairs.stem: An application stores user-uploaded files in S3. Files are frequently accessed for the first 30 days, rarely accessed for the next 60 days, then never needed again. Which S3 lifecycle configuration minimizes storage cost?
pairs.option: Transition to S3 Standard-IA at day 30; expire at 90 days total

pairs.stem: A media sharing platform lets users upload large video files from a browser. Currently all uploads pass through the application server tier before being written to S3, creating bandwidth bottlenecks and high EC2 costs during peak hours. The security team requires that upload credentials expire no more than 15 minutes after issuance. Which solution removes the application server from the upload data path while meeting the security requirement?
pairs.option: Deploy AWS Transfer Family with SFTP to accept browser-based file uploads

pairs.stem: A financial services company stores sensitive compliance reports in an S3 bucket that is accessed from multiple AWS accounts within the same AWS Organization. After an internal audit, the security team needs a control that prevents any principal outside the organization from accessing the bucket — even if an IAM policy in a member account is later misconfigured. Which S3 feature most directly satisfies this requirement?
pairs.option: S3 Block Public Access enabled at the organization's management account

pairs.stem: A healthcare startup stores de-identified patient records in S3. A new compliance framework requires (1) a verifiable log of every encryption key use, and (2) the ability to immediately revoke read access to all stored records during a security incident. The startup uses AWS KMS for key management. Which S3 server-side encryption configuration satisfies both requirements?
pairs.option: SSE-KMS with the aws/s3 AWS-managed KMS key for the account

pairs.stem: A company runs a compliance archival system where regulatory documents are uploaded once and retrieved at most once per year for audits. The compliance team's primary constraint is storage cost, not retrieval speed. Which S3 storage class is most appropriate?

nodes.title: Mixed Topics: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Mixed Topics. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: A DevOps engineer discovers that an EC2 web application is calling S3 using access keys stored in a plaintext configuration file on the instance. The security team requires these long-lived credentials to be removed immediately while preserving S3 read access. What should the solutions architect recommend?
flashcards.back: Attaching an IAM role to an EC2 instance causes the instance metadata service (IMDS) to vend temporary, automatically-rotated credentials — no static keys exist to be stolen or leaked. The application calls S3 using the same SDK calls with no code changes required. Option D still uses long-lived IAM user credentials stored on disk, which carries the same fundamental risk as the original config file; it improves secret discoverability but does not eliminate the static-credential exposure.

flashcards.front: A company's security policy requires that IAM users cannot perform any AWS API action in the current session unless they authenticated with their MFA device — not just their password — during that session. An IAM user who logs in with only username and password must be blocked from all API calls. Which control enforces this at the API request level?
flashcards.back: An IAM policy with `Effect: Deny, Action: *` and condition `aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent: false` blocks all API calls in sessions where MFA was not used, regardless of what other policies allow. The user can authenticate but cannot take any action until they use their MFA device. A password policy can require MFA device registration during account setup, but it does not enforce per-request MFA at the API level after login.

flashcards.front: A fintech company's SOC 2 audit requires that third-party auditors, who operate their own separate AWS account, have read-only access to specific S3 buckets for a two-week review window. The security team's constraints are: no long-lived credentials may be created, and no bucket endpoint may be exposed to the public internet. What should they configure?
flashcards.back: A cross-account IAM role with an S3 read-only policy and a trust policy scoped to the auditor's AWS account lets the auditors call sts:AssumeRole to obtain short-lived temporary credentials — no long-lived keys are created or shared. Deleting the role at the end of the review instantly revokes all access. Sharing IAM user access keys by email (option A) creates long-lived credentials that may be forwarded or cached, violating the no-permanent-credentials requirement. Presigned URLs (option C) are internet-accessible HTTPS endpoints — anyone who holds the URL can fetch the object — and cannot be scoped to another AWS account's identity, failing both security constraints.

flashcards.front: A web application runs on an EC2 instance with an instance profile granting s3:* on all resources and ec2:* on all resources. A security review shows the application only ever performs object retrieval from a single S3 bucket named 'prod-assets'. The team wants to reduce the blast radius if the instance is compromised. Which IAM change should a solutions architect implement?
flashcards.back: Least privilege requires granting only the exact permissions actually needed. Removing ec2:* entirely (the application makes no EC2 API calls) and replacing s3:* with s3:GetObject on the specific bucket ARN directly eliminates the excess permissions. Adding Deny statements is weaker because the broad Allow remains and implicit allow logic still grants everything not explicitly denied. A permissions boundary constrains the ceiling but does not grant or remove the underlying permissions—the role's policy still carries s3:* and ec2:*. IAM Access Analyzer flags findings but does not fix them.

pairs.stem: An e-commerce platform sends 2 million order confirmations and password-reset emails daily. The DevOps team wants to replace a self-managed Postfix relay with a fully managed AWS sending service that supports DKIM authentication, bounce and complaint processing, and delivery event notifications. Which service is the best fit?
pairs.option: Amazon SES for transactional email at scale

pairs.stem: A DevOps engineer discovers that an EC2 web application is calling S3 using access keys stored in a plaintext configuration file on the instance. The security team requires these long-lived credentials to be removed immediately while preserving S3 read access. What should the solutions architect recommend?
pairs.option: Create a dedicated IAM user and reference credentials through environment variables

pairs.stem: A genomics company runs a batch analysis pipeline on EC2 that processes 3 TB of sequencing data per job, taking 8-12 hours. The pipeline saves progress to S3 every 15 minutes and resumes from the last checkpoint after any failure. Jobs must complete eventually but have no hard deadline. Which EC2 purchasing option minimizes compute cost for this workload?
pairs.option: Dedicated Hosts reserved for a 1-year term to ensure capacity

pairs.stem: A SaaS company wants to enforce HTTPS on its public web application. Users who access the plain HTTP URL in their browser should automatically be sent to the HTTPS version. The change must be applied at the load balancer with no modifications to the application servers. Which load balancer type and configuration achieves this?
pairs.option: Application Load Balancer with an HTTP listener redirect action

pairs.stem: A DevOps engineer with full console access accidentally runs `aws cloudformation delete-stack --stack-name prod-infra` during routine maintenance, taking the production environment offline for four hours. The team wants to ensure this cannot happen again without an explicit override step. Which CloudFormation safeguard directly prevents this?
pairs.option: Enable termination protection on the stack

pairs.stem: A startup is migrating its monolith to about 20 containerized microservices. The platform team wants to avoid EC2 instance provisioning and Kubernetes cluster operations, and needs per-second billing for vCPU and memory consumed while each service container is running. Which compute option best fits their requirements?
pairs.option: Amazon EKS with self-managed EC2 node groups
